newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan 165,000 kw nuclear plant shutdown confirmed.
newsitem.headline: Japan 165,000 kw nuclear plant shutdown confirmed.

text.p: A 165,000 kilowatt advanced thermal reactor (ATR) halted operations late Tuesday night after authorities ordered the atomic reactor shut down, its operator said on Wednesday.

The Science and Technology Agency ordered the Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC) to halt operations at the plant in Tsuruga, Fukui prefecture, after it learned that the state-run body had delayed reporting a radiation leak.
The Fugen nuclear power station, along the Sea of Japan coast, northeast of Tokyo, stopped operation at 10.31 p.m. (1331 GMT) on Tuesday, a PNC spokesman said.

The radiation leak occurred when heavy water, containing the radioactive material tritium, leaked from a water purification system located in a separate building from the reactor, the PNC spokesman said.
He added that the size of the leakage was very small and had caused no damage to the environment.
The cause of the leak was a loose bolt, which has been tightened, he said.
The accident occurred on Monday, but was not reported to local or central authorities until 30 hours later.

"We deeply regret the delay in giving notification of the accident," a PNC spokesman said. "The report to authorities was delayed partly because the workers were so relieved once they found the cause of the problem. They relaxed."
The spokesman said PNC would have to wait for the authorities' permission to restart the reactor.
Three utilities -- Chubu Electric Power Co Inc, Kansai Electric Power Co Inc and Hokuriku Electric Power Co Inc -- rely on nuclear power supplies from Fugen.
The incident at the Fugen reactor, which is Japan's only heavy water reactor, has further tarnished the image of PNC management.

The state-run firm is already accused of covering up mishandling of Japan's worst nuclear accident -- a fire and explosion last month at a nuclear fuel reprocessing plant, also in Fukui. It has admitted issuing a false report about safety procedures during the incident.

In an earlier case of PNC deception in 1995, PNC officials admitted they had lied about inspections and tried to suppress videotape footage of a massive coolant leak at the firm's experimental fast-breeder reactor, Monju, which is located near the site of Monday's leakage.
The string of incidents has undermined the public's faith in nuclear power and dealt a serious blow to Japan's ambitious nuclear power policy.
Japan currently relies on nuclear power for about one-third of its power supplies, and aims to boost nuclear power dependency to 42 percent by 2010.
